tools.name: design_review
tools.title: Submit design review
tools.description: Submit an asynchronous, metered design review for a tenant-authorized HTTPS preview. This tool never edits code. Reuse client_request_id on retries, then poll design_review_get no faster than poll_after_ms.

url.description: Tenant-authorized remote preview URL. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback dev host (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1); everything else must be https. Userinfo and fragments are rejected.

routes.description: Duplicates are accepted and canonicalized by the server, so uniqueness is not required.

viewports.description: Duplicates are accepted and canonicalized by the server, so uniqueness is not required.

expected_revision.description: Optional deploy ID, commit SHA, or revision marker expected at the target.

client_request_id.description: Caller-generated idempotency key. Reuse it for retries of the same normalized request.

error.description: Typed tool error, returned with isError: true instead of the result envelope. The full code and next_action vocabularies are in schemas/review-error.schema.json.

tools.name: design_review_get
tools.title: Get design review
tools.description: Get status or a compact, focused, or evidence view for an existing review job. Poll no faster than the returned poll_after_ms. Result reads do not consume review units. Act on review.measurements.violations unconditionally: they are computed from the captured DOM and are true whether or not a model ran. Act on review.findings only when provenance.model_backed is true and coverage.state is full or partial.

grade.description: Overall verdict. Always "unjudged" when provenance.model_backed is false, and always "nothing_reviewed" when coverage.state is "nothing", which wins when both apply. No engine emits either value; the server substitutes them because nothing looked at the page, or because the run judged no route at all. Both sit deliberately outside the ship..blocked ordering so they cannot be compared against a threshold. A model-backed run CAN be "nothing_reviewed": provenance.model_backed answers whether a model was called, not whether it judged anything.

provenance.description: Where this judgment came from. Present on every review, on every backend, including the offline fixture path. A consumer reading nothing but this JSON checks it before believing anything else in the payload.

model_backed.description: true only when a vision model was called on a capture of the requested target; false when the server knows nothing judged the page; null when it cannot tell, which is the honest answer for a remote engine deployment. Treat anything other than true as not judged.

engine.description: Which adapter produced the result, e.g. bastion-fixture, verdict-cli, verdict-http.

model.description: The judge model, when one was called; null on every other path.

confidence.description: Report-backed engine confidence, or null when calibration provenance is missing, malformed, or incomplete. Always null when provenance.model_backed is false.

overall.description: The narrative assessment. When provenance.model_backed is false, or when coverage.state is "nothing", this is replaced, not annotated: prose describing a page nothing judged is never presented as a description of the target.

findings.description: The agent-facing findings. Each item is self-describing: an agent iterating this array and applying suggestion never reads the envelope, so an item from a payload nothing judged carries its own marker.

unjudged.description: Present, and always true, when nothing judged the page this finding claims to describe: the condition that also replaces grade with "unjudged" or "nothing_reviewed". Absent otherwise, so its absence claims nothing on its own and provenance and coverage stay the authority.

not_reviewed.description: Routes, viewports and previews the engine could not review, in its own words, plus this server's own disclosures. When provenance.model_backed is false the first entry begins "[bastion] no model judged this page"; when coverage.state is "nothing" an entry begins "[bastion] nothing was reviewed", after the no-model line if that one is present too.

coverage.description: What the run actually looked at. The second question a consumer asks, after provenance: an engine can honestly report model_backed true for a run whose triage named no route to review, and that run arrives as grade "ship" with an empty findings array. Route and viewport identifiers, never counts, so a caller can name what was skipped. Present on every review; state is "unstated" when the engine reported no coverage, which is never read as "everything was reviewed".

state.description: full: every requested route and viewport was reviewed. partial: something was, but not everything asked for; its grade is a real verdict about what it covered. nothing: the run judged no route, the grade is replaced with "nothing_reviewed", and nothing in the payload is an assessment of the target. unstated: the engine does not report coverage, which is disclosed rather than assumed either way.

routes_reviewed.description: Routes the run actually formed a judgment about. Empty means nothing was reviewed.

routes_skipped.description: Requested routes with no counterpart in routes_reviewed, in requested order.

measurements.description: What the run MEASURED, computed from the captured DOM with no model involved: text contrast against WCAG AA, horizontal overflow, and touch-target sizes. Present on every review. This is the one part of the payload that is true whether or not a model ran, so it is carried unchanged on unjudged and nothing-reviewed runs where grade, overall and findings are all suppressed. A measurement is never a finding: it has no severity, no confidence and no dimension, and it never changes the grade.

state.description: reported: the engine sent a measurement report. unstated: it did not, and both arrays below are empty. Read "unstated" as "this engine does not report measurements", never as "the page measured clean"; that positive statement is state "reported" with a non-empty checks_run and an empty violations.

checks_run.description: Which checks ran on this capture. Empty means nothing was measured.

violations.description: Deduped per (kind, route, element, detail), with every viewport it was measured at.

element_ref.description: Stable selector, the same vocabulary as findings[].element_ref.

detail.description: The engine's factual sentence, verbatim, e.g. "text contrast 3.23:1 is below WCAG AA 4.5:1".

block_eligible.description: The ENGINE's claim that this measurement is precise enough to gate a merge on. false does not mean the measurement is wrong, only that acting on it automatically would be: it may be intentional (a deliberate scroll container, a desktop pointer target) or in a known false-positive class (text over a background image).

hallucination_drops.description: How many model findings the engine's grounding gate deleted for citing a route or an element the capture never produced, or null when the engine reported no grounding gate. null and 0 are different answers: 0 means the gate ran and deleted nothing. A positive value with an empty findings array is not a clean page, it is a page the model had things to say about, none of which could be pointed at. It never suppresses the grade: the routes were judged and the gate did its job.

presentation.description: Emitted by the evidence view only: the honest capability downgrade, naming exactly what the calling host could not render rather than dropping it silently.

panel.description: The interactive MCP-Apps HTML panel was emitted as a resource block.

panel_withheld.description: A panel was available but withheld because the host lacks MCP-Apps support.

multimedia.description: At least one annotated image block was emitted.

images_withheld.description: evidence_ids whose annotated image was withheld for a non-multimedia host.

error.description: Typed tool error, returned with isError: true instead of the result envelope. The full code and next_action vocabularies are in schemas/review-error.schema.json.

tools.name: design_recheck
tools.title: Submit design recheck
tools.description: Submit a metered recheck for findings from a completed review after the customer's agent changes the UI. This tool never edits code. Unchanged targets and exhausted recheck loops are rejected without running judgment. Check recheck.provenance before acting: when nothing judged the target every outcome is unjudged with a null confidence. Reuse client_request_id on retries.

items.description: A finding_id from the review being rechecked. The floor is 3, not 8: ids come from the engine's own review result and are as short as "f_001".

finding_ids.description: Duplicates are accepted and canonicalized by the server, so uniqueness is not required.

url.description: Optional URL on the same previously authorized host. A host change requires a new review. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback dev host (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1).

outcome.description: Per-finding verdict. Always "unjudged" when provenance.model_backed is false: no engine emits that value, the server substitutes it because nothing observed the target, and it is deliberately distinct from "inconclusive", which means something looked and could not tell.

confidence.description: Engine confidence in this outcome, or null when there is no verdict to be confident about. Always null when the outcome is "unjudged".

reason.description: Why the outcome is what it is. When provenance.model_backed is false this is replaced, not annotated, and begins "[bastion] no model judged this page": a sentence asserting the issue is no longer observed at the target is never presented for a target nothing observed.

provenance.description: Where this recheck came from. Present on every recheck, on every backend, including the offline fixture path. A recheck is what an agent reads to decide its fix landed and it can stop working, so it checks this before believing any outcome below.

model_backed.description: true only when a vision model was called on a capture of the requested target; false when the server knows nothing judged the page; null when it cannot tell, which is the honest answer for a remote engine deployment. Treat anything other than true as not judged.

engine.description: Which adapter produced the result, e.g. bastion-fixture, verdict-cli, verdict-http.

model.description: The judge model, when one was called; null on every other path.

error.description: Typed tool error, returned with isError: true instead of the result envelope. The full code and next_action vocabularies are in schemas/review-error.schema.json.

tools.name: design_review_cancel
tools.title: Cancel design review
tools.description: Request best-effort cancellation of a queued or running review job. Terminal jobs keep their existing state. Cancellation does not edit customer systems and consumes no review units.

error.description: Typed tool error, returned with isError: true instead of the result envelope. The full code and next_action vocabularies are in schemas/review-error.schema.json.

tools.name: design_review_panel_action
tools.title: Act on a review panel finding
tools.description: Route an interaction from the interactive review panel: return a grounded finding's fix for the coding agent to apply, or the refs to re-verify. This tool never edits code. An advisory finding returns human_only, never an automatic fix, and a review nothing judged returns unjudged with no fix at all. Reads only; consumes no review units.

provenance.description: Where the review this action was routed from came from. A routed fix is a string the caller is expected to act on, so the payload says in-band whether anything judged the review that produced it. When model_backed is false, response.type is "unjudged" and no fix is returned.

model_backed.description: true only when a vision model was called on a capture of the requested target; false when the server knows nothing judged the page; null when it cannot tell, which is the honest answer for a remote engine deployment. Treat anything other than true as not judged.

engine.description: Which adapter produced the result, e.g. bastion-fixture, verdict-cli, verdict-http.

model.description: The judge model, when one was called; null on every other path.

response.description: The panel reducer's routed response: a grounded fix for the coding agent, a human_only referral, an unjudged refusal when nothing judged the review, or the recheck refs.

type.description: "unjudged" is returned for apply_fix whenever provenance.model_backed is false: there is no fix to hand over and no advisory judgment to refer to a human, so neither is invented.

error.description: Typed tool error, returned with isError: true instead of the result envelope. The full code and next_action vocabularies are in schemas/review-error.schema.json.
